title: Taking the Employee's Own Stored Value into Account against a Charge to Pay
content:
Value the employee already holds on their Employee Meal Account is taken into account against what is carried to their pay, and how much of it is taken into account turns on whether the account has lately run short at the till.

**Clause.** Where the stored value standing on the account is at least the smallest single load the plan accepts and no overdraft charge has been raised on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the stored value taken into account is the whole of the stored value standing. Where the stored value standing is at least that smallest single load and an overdraft charge has been raised on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the stored value taken into account is the stored value standing less the overdraft limit printed against the plan, never read as less than nothing. Where neither holds, no stored value is taken into account.

## The plan figures this reads

| Meal plan | Smallest single load the plan accepts | Overdraft limit on one transaction |
|---|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | $0.00 | $0.00 |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | $10.00 | $15.00 |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | $5.00 | $25.00 |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | $5.00 | $10.00 |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | $0.00 | $0.00 |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | $20.00 | $150.00 |

## The bands

| Stored value standing | Overdraft charges raised in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | Taken into account |
|---|---|---|
| At least the plan's smallest single load | None | The whole of the stored value standing |
| At least the plan's smallest single load | 1 or more | The stored value standing less the plan's overdraft limit, never below nothing |
| Below the plan's smallest single load | Either | Nothing |

*Hypothetical illustration.* An account holding $90.00 of stored value on a plan whose smallest single load is $5.00 and whose overdraft limit is $25.00: with no overdraft charge in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, $90.00 is taken into account; with one, $65.00. An account holding $18.00 on a plan whose overdraft limit is $25.00, with an overdraft charge in that month, has nothing taken into account, since $18.00 less $25.00 is never read as less than nothing.
